title: Constant-coefficient realization of the etale/pro-etale ringed square
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and $p:X	o Y$ any morphism of schemes. Use small representatives of their etale and pro-etale sites in the common universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $R_{T,s}=\underline A_{T_s}$ for the constant ring sheaf, normalized by its constant sections [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Equip $p_{\mathrm{et}},p_{\mathrm{proet}},
u_X,
u_Y$ with the structure-ring maps $c_w:w^{-1}R_{\mathrm{target}}	o R_{\mathrm{source}}$ preserving every constant section [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $c_R$ be the geometric commutation comparison $
u_X^{-1}p_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}R_{Y,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}p_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}
u_Y^{-1}R_{Y,\mathrm{et}}$ induced by base change of site objects.
All four $c_w$ are isomorphisms, and the structural maps satisfy
$$c_{
u_X}\circ
u_X^{-1}(c_{p_{\mathrm{et}}})=c_{p_{\mathrm{proet}}}\circ p_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}(c_{
u_Y})\circ c_R.$$
Thus this specified geometric square is a commutative square of ringed topoi; cartesianness is not asserted. Under the constant-section-preserving equivalences between fixed-$A$ module sheaves and $R_{T,s}$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-constant-ring-equivalence], the induced module commutation comparison preserves zero, addition and each scalar action and equals the specified fixed-coefficient comparison. In ordinary uncompleted derived categories put $F_T=
u_T^*$, $u=p_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ and $v=p_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$. The ringed square's derived comparison $	heta:vF_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Xu$ is precisely $a^{-1}$, where $a:F_Xu\xrightarrow{\sim}vF_Y$ is the termwise localization of the ordinary fixed-$A$ module comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to these uncompleted derived categories, as an equality of the specified natural isomorphisms under these equivalences.

proof.text: For each original site use its terminal object. The composite of the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction with the edge ring-sheaf adjunction has the same right adjoint as the constant-sheaf adjunction on the destination. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives an invertible map. The Hom-equivalence computation identifies its component with ringMap, since both adjuncts are the extension of the constant-section sheafification unit. This proves ringMap_isIso, including for the empty scheme and the zero ring.

Transpose the two coefficient-square paths through the composite ring adjunctions. The unit equation for the conjugate comparison changes the desired equality into equality of the two composite direct-section maps. The sheafification adjunction detects it after precomposition by the constant-presheaf unit. Apply ringDirectMap_unit on each edge; both sides are then the same constant section on the same chosen base change.

source.place: Tag 09A5, square before Tag 09A6; sites.tex Tag 0H7J

proof.text: Restricting module scalars through the constant sections identifies modulePush followed by restriction with restriction followed by fixedPush: construct directComparisonAux by identity linear maps on sections, using ringDirectMap_unit to check scalar linearity. The constant-ring restriction is an additive equivalence. Transport the fixed-coefficient adjunction across it to prove modulePushIsRightAdjoint. The inverse mate of the identity-section comparison is invertible because both vertical functors are equivalences. Its unit equation and injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence prove pullComparison_existsUnique; sectionwise extensionality proves directComparison_existsUnique.

Paste the two directComparisonAux isomorphisms on each path with the canonical fixed-coefficient direct-image square. Cancel the fully faithful constant-ring restriction to obtain squareDirectComparison; it is identity on sections, which also proves uniqueness. Apply the mates equivalence to the desired ordinary square. Compatibility of mates with horizontal and vertical composition reduces it to the equality of these identity-section direct-image comparisons. Cancel the inverse pullComparison components to obtain precisely ordinary.

The fixed-coefficient inverse images are additive and exact. Transport additivity and finite limits through pullComparison and the faithful constant-ring equivalence; finite colimits follow from the actual module adjunction. Apply the exact-derived square-composition theorem to each two-edge path, with their common ordinary comparison q. The ordinary equation supplies its hypothesis on the second path. Cancel the common derived composition factors to identify the forward derived squares, and invert that equation to get the stated theta = a inverse with all four specified derivedPullComparison factors. All functors here are termwise localizations on the ordinary unbounded derived categories.
